cards.task: Find the key, pick it up, open the locked door, go into the room, and then pick up the ball.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the locked door, then waits outside.
Takes the key, then waits: the locked door is never opened.

paraphrases: First find the key and then pick it up. After that, open the locked door, enter the room, and then pick up the ball.
Locate the key and take it, unlock and open the door, step into the room, and finish by picking up the ball.
Find the key, take it, open the locked door, walk into the room behind it, and then pick up the ball.
cards.notes: Five ordered steps (long sequence). Every order is forced by the env, so only the last step can fail. Changed in card fix 2: the four orders are optional extras in scoring (`forced`); Existence(target_picked_up) alone is also a correct output. `key_found` now needs a clear view of the key. Order audit 2026-11-20: the list "..., go into the room, and then pick up the ball" states all four orders, and a stated order is required even when the level forces it, so `forced` is gone, Existence(target_picked_up) alone is no longer correct, and the answer with one Existence per step (no order) left `also_ok`. p1 ("First ... Then ...") and p2 ("... and finish by picking up the ball") state the same orders; p3 lists the steps with no order word. Card fixes 2026-11-20: p3 now ends "..., and then pick up the ball.", the form of the task, so it states the four orders it is scored for. p1 now reads "First find the key and then pick it up. After that, open the locked door, enter the room, and then pick up the ball.": its second sentence was a list with no order word, which states no order among the door, the room and the ball (the reading of base-unlock-pickup). p2 is unchanged: its list ends with "and finish by", like the task's "and then". Moved from KeyCorridorS6R3 to KeyCorridorS4R3 on 2026-11-20 (with base-key-corridor): no method learned S6R3 in 71 runs. Before the move, `target_room_entered` used S6R3's 6x6 rooms and turned true outside the room, before the locked door opened, on S4R3: in the reference labeler in 106 of 300 random episodes of turns, moves and toggles (the train probe's `room_entered_check.py`), and in the generated labelings in 155 of 300 random episodes that also pick up and drop (`check/room_size_check.py` in the facts folder). The facts page and the reference labeler now read the room size from `env.room_size`. The FARM bundle and its three paraphrases were generated again on S4R3 (production pair, `--reasoning high`, end judgment off: the default `reward_end_judgment`), and FARM learned this card on 3 of 3 seeds (judged success 0.91, 0.81, 0.87 at 1.5M steps), no-RM on none (0.00 on all three). `expect` and the answer lists are unchanged. ARM-FM, 2026-11-20: the four ARM-FM bundles still have the S6R3 page and room geometry; `run-suite` refuses them (bundle level mismatch), and they are generated again at the freeze.

cards.task: Do not pick up the box in the other room. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Whenever you are holding the key, try to have the door open at that moment or open it afterwards.

wrong.why: Moves the ball, takes the key and opens the door, then picks up the box.
Takes the key first and has to drop it with the door closed to move the ball, then opens the door.
Moves the ball and takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.

paraphrases: Never pick up the box in the other room. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed, and whenever you hold the key, try to have the door open then or open it later.
Leave the box alone. Whenever you are holding the key, try to have the door open at that moment or open it afterwards, and try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.
Do not take the box from the other room. At any moment you hold the key, try to have the door open then or open it afterwards, and try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.
cards.notes: Rules only, no goal: one hard ban and two soft rules. Moved from DoorKey to BlockedUnlockPickup in the D10 revision: a key-first run has to drop the key with the door closed to move the ball, so the soft key rule binds. Changed in card fix 2: the soft door rule is worded as the state it checks (the judge needs the door open when you last hold the key or later), instead of the event reading. Card fixes 2026-11-18: doing nothing passes every hard and soft clause (no box pickup, no key drop, no key held), so report the idle baseline and how often the key rule fires beside the judged success. Kept trained for now: it is the ablation suite's small card and its FARM run is that suite's control; the Lanes level (`lanes-rules`) is meant to replace it. S2 2026-11-19: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) is not an `also_ok` answer for the soft Absence(key_lost): it is weaker, it accepts opening the door, shutting it again and dropping the key, which the wording forbids. Card fixes 2026-11-20: stopped training (`train: false`, and out of `closed-set.json`). An idle agent passes it, and `lanes-rules` replaced it in the ablation suite on 2026-11-19 and covers rules with no goal. It stays a generation card.

cards.task: Open the door and then pick up the box in the other room, and try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.

wrong.why: Takes the key first and has to drop it with the door closed to move the ball, then finishes.
Moves the ball, takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

paraphrases: Pick up the box in the other room after opening the door, and try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.
Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Open the door, then pick up the box in the other room.
Open the door, then take the box from the other room; try not to drop the key while the door is still closed.
cards.notes: Goal of two steps plus one soft rule; the soft rule is not in the env reward. Moved from UnlockPickup to BlockedUnlockPickup in the D10 revision, so it sits on the same world as cx-goal-many-rules: a key-first run has to drop the key with the door closed to move the ball. Changed in card fix 2: the hard door-before-box order is forced by the world, so it is an optional extra in scoring (`forced`). S2 2026-11-19: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) is not an `also_ok` answer for the soft Absence(key_lost): it is weaker, it accepts opening the door, shutting it again and dropping the key, which the wording forbids. Order audit 2026-11-20: "open the door and then pick up the box" states the order (every paraphrase says "then" or "after"), and a stated order is required even when the level forces it, so `forced` is gone and the answer with Existence(door_open) and Existence(target_picked_up) but no order left `also_ok`. The Response answer stays: it states the order as "after the door, the box". Card fixes 2026-11-20: the Response answer left `also_ok` too. `Response` is not a step form, so it does not carry the stated order (user rule); the answer with the `Precedence` and both Existences stays.

cards.task: Move the ball away from the door before you take the key. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. Whenever you are holding the key, try to have the door open at that moment or open it afterwards. Then open the door with the key and pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Takes the key first and has to drop it with the door closed, then finishes.
Moves the ball first, but drops the key once with the door closed, then finishes.
Moves the ball and takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.

paraphrases: Before taking the key, move the ball away from the door. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed, and whenever you are holding the key, try to have the door open at that moment or open it afterwards. Finally, open the door with the key and pick up the box in the other room.

Take the key only after the ball is out of the way. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed. At any moment you are holding the key, try to have the door open then or open it later. Then use the key to open the door and get the box from the other room.

First clear the ball from the door and only then take the key. Try not to drop the key while the door is still closed, and whenever you hold the key, try to have the door open at that moment or open it afterwards. After that, open the door with the key and pick up the box in the other room.
cards.notes: One hard rule, two soft rules and a two-step goal. Changed in card fix 2: the soft door rule is worded as the state it checks (the judge needs the door open when you last hold the key or later, so closing the door again while still holding the key leaves the rule open), and the hard door-before-box order is an optional extra in scoring (`forced`). Card fixes 2026-11-18: the soft key-drop ban is unforced once the hard ball-first order is obeyed (a ball-first run never has to drop the key with the door closed), so it is not a second binding trade-off. S2 2026-11-19: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) is not an `also_ok` answer for the soft Absence(key_lost): it is weaker, it accepts opening the door, shutting it again and dropping the key, which the wording forbids. Chain reword 2026-11-19: the task names every step ("open the door with the key"), so the hard answer is the chain Existence(box), Precedence(door_open, box), Precedence(has_door_key, door_open) plus the card's own Precedence(blocker_moved, has_door_key); both chain orders are forced by the level (`forced`), and the progress pay reads the machine, so a step with no rule of its own would pay nothing. 2026-11-20: the answer with Precedence(door_open, box), Existence(blocker_moved) and Existence(box) but no Existence(has_door_key) left `also_ok`: it has no key step, so the soft Response charges the key pickup -1 with nothing to offset it (about 1 seed in 3 never learns it). The answer with Existence(blocker_moved) and Existence(box) but no key or door step left too, for the same trap (solve pay 1, -1, 1, 11; never trained). Order audit 2026-11-20: "Then open the door with the key and pick up the box" states both chain orders (the key opens the door; the steps after "Then" are a sequence, as the paraphrases' "Finally" and "After that" say), and a stated order is required even when the level forces it, so `forced` is gone and the four remaining `also_ok` answers left: none has Precedence(has_door_key, door_open), and two also lack Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up).

cards.task: Go to the exit, and whenever the siren rings, turn it off.

wrong.why: Ignores the siren and walks to the exit with it still ringing.

paraphrases: Reach the exit. Each time the siren rings, switch it off.
Every time the siren rings, turn it off with the switch, and get to the exit.
Make your way to the exit, and silence the siren every time it rings.
cards.notes: Event room, siren rule. The env reward needs the siren silent at the exit.

cards.task: Carry the box to the exit, and whenever the box falls, pick it up again.

wrong.why: Does not react to the fall and walks to the exit without the box.
Walks straight to the exit and never touches the box.

paraphrases: Take the box to the exit. Each time the box falls, pick it up again.
Every time the box falls, pick it up again, and reach the exit with the box in your hands.
Make your way to the exit carrying the box, and pick the box up again every time it falls.
cards.notes: Event room, box rule. Changed in card fix 2: the task asks to carry the box to the exit, checked at the exit step (Response(at_exit, holding_box)), so a direct exit no longer passes; the recovery rule stays as an additional rule (the pickup may come later than the next move). The env reward at the exit also needs the box; judged success is the metric here.
